outcome: No source I could read settles the measure classification as of 11 Oct 2026. Since 26 Jan 2024 the only in-window work touching it is partial and neighbouring: Hochman (arXiv 2609.21481, 18 Sep 2026) proves a zero-entropy dense-orbit theorem that he says does not resolve the problem, Burton and Juschenko (arXiv 2610.04745, 3 Oct 2026) prove entropy-rate constraints on potential counterexamples, and both state the problem open; an undated HAL preprint claiming a 'low-tech proof' could not be opened.
problem_asks: Let T2: x -> 2x mod 1 and T3: x -> 3x mod 1 act on the circle R/Z. Parts: (1) for every probability measure mu on the circle invariant under both T2 and T3 and ergodic for the semigroup they generate, is mu Lebesgue measure; (2) if mu is not Lebesgue, is mu atomic (purely atomic, equivalently finitely supported for an ergodic measure); (3) the bullet asks for the dichotomy as a whole, 'either Lebesgue or atomic'. Atomic examples exist (uniform measures on finite orbits of rationals whose denominators are coprime to 6), so the open content is the exclusion of every other ergodic joint-invariant measure. Not asked by the bullet: the closed-set version (infinite closed invariant sets are the whole circle, Furstenberg 1967), the intersection-dimension conjecture, or the generalisation to other multiplicatively independent pairs (a, b), which the literature states but the bullet does not. Non-ergodic joint-invariant measures reduce to the ergodic case by ergodic decomposition (Tal's survey). The Wikipedia wording is 'either Lebesgue or atomic'; the literature's ergodic form is 'mu = lambda or supp(mu) is a finite set' (Tal 2021; Burton and Panangaden 2024); Hochman (2026) states it as 'the only non-atomic, jointly invariant probability measure on [0,1] is Lebesgue'. I did not verify those forms are equivalent in detail.

events.what_happened: H. Furstenberg (1967) proved that an infinite closed subset of the circle invariant under x -> 2x and x -> 3x mod 1 is the whole circle. This is the set-level analogue that motivated the measure question; it is a different question (closed sets, not measures). Reported in Tal's survey (arXiv 2110.05989) and in the Hillel Furstenberg biography, which cites the 1967 paper 'Disjointness in ergodic theory, minimal sets, and a problem in Diophantine approximation'. The original 1967 paper was not opened.
events.delivers: Closed-set version only: every infinite closed set invariant under both maps is the whole circle. Says nothing about invariant measures.
events.remains: The whole measure question: classification of ergodic jointly invariant probability measures into Lebesgue or atomic.

checked_by.who: Furstenberg's 1967 paper (journal of publication not verified in my sources)
checked_by.qualification: Author of the theorem; refereed publication of the era
checked_by.what_they_did: Proved the set-level theorem; later surveys reproduce it (Tal 2021)

events.direction: Rigidity holds for closed sets, in the direction the measure conjecture predicts for measures; it does not decide the measure version.

events.what_happened: R. Lyons, 'On measures simultaneously 2- and 3-invariant', Israel J. Math. 61(2) (1988), 219-224 (volume and pages from two reference lists in search results). Per Tal's survey quoting Lyons: if a nonzero measure mu on the circle is invariant under x -> px and x -> qx (p, q coprime) and K-mixing for x -> px, then mu is Lebesgue. Lyons also stated conjectures that later work disputes (see the Kazhdan-constants event).
events.delivers: Lebesgue measure, under the extra hypothesis that mu is K-mixing for one of the two maps. The class is restricted to K-mixing measures.
events.remains: All ergodic joint-invariant measures that are not K-mixing for either map, including every zero-entropy one.

checked_by.where: Bibliographic entries in search results; the paper itself was not opened

events.direction: Toward the Lebesgue side, under a K-mixing hypothesis.

events.what_happened: D. J. Rudolph, '×2 and ×3 invariant measures and entropy', Ergodic Theory Dynam. Systems 10 (1990), 395-406 (received Sept 1987, revised Oct 1989; DOI 10.1017/s0143385700005629). Result per search metadata and Tal's survey: if mu is invariant under x -> 2x and x -> 3x and ergodic for the semigroup, and some element of the semigroup has positive entropy with respect to mu, then mu is Lebesgue; equivalently, if mu is not Lebesgue then both maps have zero entropy with respect to mu. The preprint date is not established, so the year of the journal volume is used. The Cambridge PDF was not readable by my tools.
events.delivers: Lebesgue measure, under positive entropy for some element of the semigroup and ergodicity for the semigroup. This settles the positive-entropy part of the bullet's dichotomy for ergodic joint-invariant measures.
events.remains: The zero-entropy case: a non-Lebesgue ergodic joint-invariant measure whose entropy is zero for both maps. Every 2026 source I read says this case is open.

checked_by.who: Ergodic Theory and Dynamical Systems (refereed journal)
checked_by.qualification: Journal of record; the result is widely cited
checked_by.where: https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/64243AD8323B37089540F911F8CC77EB/S0143385700005629a.pdf/2-and-3-invariant-measures-and-entropy.pdf (PDF not readable by my tools; metadata only)

checked_by.what_they_did: Gave alternative proofs of the positive-entropy case, per Tal's survey (not opened)

events.direction: Toward the Lebesgue side, under positive entropy; leaves the zero-entropy side open.

events.what_happened: A. S. A. Johnson (PhD Maryland 1990 under Rudolph, per Math Genealogy), 'Measures on the circle invariant under multiplication by a nonlacunary subsemigroup of the integers', Israel J. Math. 77 (1992), 211-240 (DOI 10.1007/BF02808018). Per the journal abstract as quoted in search results: for a nonlacunary subsemigroup S and an S-invariant ergodic measure, positive entropy with respect to some element of S forces Lebesgue measure. Tal's survey and Hochman (2026) credit it as extending Rudolph to multiplicatively independent integers.
events.delivers: Lebesgue measure under positive entropy for some element of a nonlacunary semigroup. For the bullet's pair (2, 3), this is the same positive-entropy case as Rudolph's theorem.
events.remains: The zero-entropy case for the pair (2, 3).

checked_by.where: https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02808018 (DOI from search results; not opened)

events.direction: Toward the Lebesgue side, under positive entropy.

events.what_happened: B. Host, 'Nombres normaux, entropie, translations', Israel J. Math. 91 (1995), 419-428. Per a talk abstract and slides quoted in search results: for coprime p, q, a ×p-invariant ergodic measure with positive entropy has almost every point normal in base q (Fourier-analytic method). This is a normality statement about generic points, not a classification of invariant measures.
events.delivers: Normality of almost every point for ×p-invariant ergodic measures of positive entropy. It is a related property on the positive-entropy side; it does not identify the measure.
events.remains: The classification itself, including the zero-entropy case.

checked_by.where: Bibliographic entry in search results; the paper was not opened

events.direction: Neither side of the classification; a positive-entropy normality result that is discussed alongside the bullet.

events.what_happened: T. Downarowicz and S. Huczek (initials not verified), 'Empirical approach to the ×2,×3 conjecture', arXiv 1901.01452 (January 2019); journal version in Experimental Mathematics (vol. 31, no. 1 per a search result; year not verified). The paper uses software to search for atomic invariant measures on finite orbits and identifies 'outlier' measures whose supports are far from uniformly distributed; it suggests that a sequence of atomic measures might converge to a non-Lebesgue invariant measure. The paper was not opened; the description comes from search summaries.
events.delivers: No theorem. Computational evidence about the distribution of finite-orbit atomic invariant measures, and a heuristic about possible non-Lebesgue limits.
events.remains: All of the bullet.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the journal version (per a search result)

events.direction: No direct cut. The search suggests atomic measures are abundant and might have non-Lebesgue limits; this is a heuristic, not a counterexample, and atomic measures are allowed by the bullet.

events.what_happened: M. Wu, 'A proof of Furstenberg's conjecture on the intersections of ×p- and ×q-invariant sets', arXiv 1609.08053 (September 2016), Annals of Math. 189(3) (2019), 707-751. Shmerkin posted an independent proof, arXiv 1609.07802 (September 2016), Annals 189(3) (2019). Both prove the 1969 intersection conjecture: a dimension bound for intersections of ×p- and ×q-invariant closed sets. This is a different problem from the measure classification.
events.revisions: Multiple arXiv versions (v2, v3 seen in search results; dates not checked). Published Annals of Math. 2019.
events.delivers: A dimension bound for slices of ×p- and ×q-invariant closed subsets of [0,1] when log p / log q is irrational. It says nothing about invariant measures classified as Lebesgue or atomic.
events.remains: The whole measure classification.
events.direction: No cut on the measure question. It is a neighbouring problem in Furstenberg's programme.

events.what_happened: T. Austin, 'A new dynamical proof of the Shmerkin-Wu theorem', arXiv 2009.01292 (September 2020). A third proof of the same intersection-dimension result as the Wu and Shmerkin papers. No journal publication was found. Seminar listings describe it as a simple proof of the intersection conjecture.
events.delivers: A new proof of the closed-set intersection dimension bound. A different problem from the measure classification.
events.remains: The whole measure classification.
events.direction: No cut on the measure question.

events.what_happened: F. Manners, 'A solution to the Pyjama Problem', arXiv 1305.1514 (submitted 7 May 2013; Inventiones Math. 202 (2015)). Shows that finitely many rotations of a pyjama stripe cover the plane. The proof follows the Furstenberg ×2×3 argument by analogy; it is a planar covering problem, not the measure classification. Per search summaries, Kravitz and Leng later gave quantitative bounds.
events.delivers: Covering of the plane by finitely many rotations of the pyjama stripe, for every positive width. Only analogous to the bullet.
events.remains: The whole bullet; this is a different question.
events.direction: No cut on the measure question; it is an analogue.

events.what_happened: arXiv 1804.01369, 'Kazhdan constants, continuous probability measures with large Fourier coefficients and rigidity sequences' (April 2018; authors not recorded, not opened). Per a search summary: constructs a continuous probability measure on the circle whose Fourier coefficients stay bounded away from zero along the set {2^k 3^l}, and so disproves a 1988 conjecture of Lyons inspired by the ×2×3 question. The Badea-Grivaux talk abstract also reports a disproof of a Lyons conjecture (C3).
events.delivers: Refutes a neighbouring Fourier-coefficient conjecture of Lyons. It is not a statement about the classification.
events.remains: The whole bullet.
events.direction: No direct cut on the classification; refutes a neighbouring conjecture.
events.object: A continuous probability measure on the circle whose Fourier coefficients are bounded away from zero along {2^k 3^l} (per search summary; not opened).

events.what_happened: C. Badea and S. Grivaux, 'Around Furstenberg's times p, times q conjecture: times p-invariant measures with some large Fourier coefficients', arXiv 2303.01089 (v1 2 Mar 2023; v2 17 Sep 2024; v3 6 Nov 2024); Discrete Analysis 2024:10 (DOI 10.19086/da.124611). Baire-category argument: for multiplicatively independent p, q, a generic atomless T_p-invariant probability measure has large Fourier coefficients along powers of q, so the pushforwards T_(q^n) mu do not converge weak-star to Lebesgue. This disproves Furstenberg's conjecture on that convergence (the journal's editorial introduction says 'the main aim of this paper is to disprove this last conjecture'). It concerns T_p alone, not joint invariance.
events.revisions: v2 17 Sep 2024; v3 6 Nov 2024 (in window); published Discrete Analysis 2024.
events.delivers: Negative answer to a neighbouring Furstenberg conjecture about convergence of T_(q^n) mu to Lebesgue for atomless T_p-invariant measures. It does not treat measures invariant under both maps.
events.remains: The whole bullet.
events.direction: No cut on the classification. It refutes a neighbouring conjecture on convergence of iterated pushforwards.
events.object: A generic (Baire-category) atomless T_p-invariant probability measure on the circle with large Fourier coefficients along powers of q. Existence is non-constructive, by a Baire-category argument.

events.what_happened: P. Burton and J. Panangaden, 'Formulations of Furstenberg's ×2×3 conjecture in complex analysis and operator algebras', arXiv 2410.22701 (submitted 30 Oct 2024; one version). Gives equivalent reformulations: nine conjectures in three triples, on Caratheodory functions on the unit disk with a functional identity and on tracial states of the full group C*-algebra of a Baumslag-Solitar-type semidirect product. Relates the conjecture to a periodic approximation question (Levit and Vigdorovich) and a periodic equidistribution conjecture (Lindenstrauss). A 2025 Caltech seminar abstract describes the same joint project. The arXiv abstract states that the conjecture 'has been a central open problem in ergodic theory for over 50 years'. A journal version exists in a Springer journal in 2026 (DOI 10.1007/s43034-026-00512-1); the page redirected to a login and was not read.
events.revisions: v1 only on arXiv (30 Oct 2024); Springer journal version 2026 (not read).
events.delivers: Equivalent reformulations of the conjecture in two other settings. Per the search summary, one of the stated results is that a conjecture in the paper implies another. No new partial result on the measure classification is claimed in the abstract.
events.remains: The whole bullet.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the journal version (2026); referee process not visible

events.direction: Neither side: reformulation only.

events.what_happened: A. Algom, M. Hochman and M. Wu, 'New results on embeddings of self-similar sets via renormalization', arXiv 2410.19648 (October 2024; day not established). Works on the affine embedding conjecture of Feng, Huang and Rao and its weak intersection form. Per search summaries, it implies the intersection conjecture in the homogeneous case and makes partial progress in the non-homogeneous case. Published in Proc. London Math. Soc. 133 (2026) according to a repository listing. The arXiv page was not opened.
events.delivers: Partial results on embeddings and intersections of self-similar sets. Not about invariant measures on the circle.
events.remains: The whole bullet.

checked_by.who: Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society (refereed journal)
checked_by.qualification: Journal of record (per a repository listing)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper (2026, per the listing)
checked_by.where: Oulu repository listing (search result; not opened)

events.direction: No cut on the measure question. A neighbouring intersection/embedding problem.

events.what_happened: N. Kravitz and J. Leng, 'Quantitative pyjama', arXiv 2510.17744 (20 Oct 2025). Shows that exp(exp(exp(ε^(-O(1))))) rotations of a pyjama stripe cover the plane, using entropic tools from Bourgain, Lindenstrauss, Michel and Venkatesh for quantitative ×2,×3-type results. Its abstract does not name Furstenberg's problem or the measure conjecture.
events.delivers: A quantitative covering bound for the pyjama problem. It is an analogue, not the bullet.
events.remains: The whole bullet.
events.direction: No cut on the measure question; an analogue.

events.what_happened: H. Zhao, 'Generic Zero-Entropy Optimization for Finitely Generated Nonlacunary Actions on the Circle', arXiv 2608.24503 (v1 25 Aug 2026; v2 31 Aug 2026). For a finitely generated nonlacunary multiplicative semigroup, a dense set of potentials has maximising and minimising invariant measures of zero entropy; the proof uses Rudolph-Johnson entropy rigidity. The abstract says the result applies to simultaneous T_p, T_q invariance for multiplicatively independent p, q. It is an optimisation statement, not a classification.
events.revisions: v1 25 Aug 2026; v2 31 Aug 2026 (main theorem extended from Lipschitz to W^{1,s} potentials, sharpness added).
events.delivers: For a dense set of potentials, the optimising invariant measures have zero entropy for every nontrivial element of the semigroup. This is a statement about maximisers of integrals, not about classifying invariant measures.
events.remains: The whole bullet.
events.direction: No cut on the classification. It states a zero-entropy conclusion for optimisers.

events.what_happened: A. Algom, 'Ergodic ×p-invariant measures on T^2 with no dimension dropping projections', arXiv 2608.29569 (v1 30 Aug 2026). Constructs, for p >= 2 and 0 < s < 1, an ergodic ×p-invariant measure on T^2 of dimension s whose line projections all preserve dimension; shows that quasi-Bernoulli ×p-invariant measures with positive entropy have a dimension-dropping projection. The introduction cites Furstenberg's ×2×3 problem only as a guiding principle (Section 1.3). The paper does not state or classify ×2×3-invariant measures on the circle.
events.delivers: Dimension results for a single ×p-invariant measure on T^2 and its projections. It does not address joint invariance under ×2 and ×3 on the circle.
events.remains: The whole bullet.
events.direction: No cut on the classification.
events.object: An ergodic ×p-invariant measure on T^2 of dimension s (0 < s < 1) with no dimension-dropping line projections, with tube bound mu(T) <= C w(T)^s. Whether the construction is explicit or non-constructive was not verified from the abstract.

events.what_happened: M. Hochman, 'Dense times-b orbits from times-a invariant sets and measures, in zero entropy', arXiv 2609.21481 (submitted 18 Sep 2026; v1 only). Theorem 1.2: for multiplicatively independent integers a, b >= 2 and a non-atomic, ergodic, ×a-invariant probability measure mu on [0,1], mu-almost every x has a dense ×b-orbit; the author notes this covers zero entropy, positive entropy being Host's theorem. Corollary 1.3 treats a-sets. Theorem 1.9 gives analogues for commuting toral matrices. The paper's introduction states the ×2,×3 problem as 'the only non-atomic, jointly-Ta,Tb-invariant probability measure on [0,1] is Lebesgue', and says 'the problem remains open; although an affirmative answer was given by Rudolph and Johnson for measures with positive Ta-entropy, nothing is known in entropy zero'. It says a positive answer to the problem would not yield the zero-entropy theorem, and that upgrading transitivity to normality 'would resolve the ×2,×3-problem' but the methods are 'far too crude'. Hochman gave a talk, 'Around the x2,x3 question', at HUJI on 5 May 2026 with the same result; the date is the write-up date per the rule. AI disclosure (Section 1.6): 'ChatGPT 5.6 Terra was used to help locate errata.' 'Resulting corrections were done out manually.' 'The author takes full responsibility for the content.' This is errata-location (checking), so it is not in ai.systems; see summary. Funding: ISF 3056/21; Warwick hospitality 2024/5.
events.delivers: For non-atomic ergodic ×a-invariant measures on [0,1] with a, b multiplicatively independent: almost every point has a dense ×b-orbit, including in zero entropy. It does not assume ×b-invariance of the measure and does not classify jointly invariant measures. The author says the problem is open and that a positive answer would not give this theorem.
events.remains: The whole bullet: the classification of jointly invariant ergodic measures, including the zero-entropy case, which the author says is unknown.
events.direction: No cut on the classification as such. A dense-orbit property holds for Lebesgue measure but does not force it, and fails for atomic measures on finite orbits, so the result is compatible with the Lebesgue side but does not identify any measure. The author explicitly says the problem is open.

events.what_happened: P. Burton and K. Juschenko, 'Entropic rates from eigenfunction structure for ×2×3', arXiv 2610.04745 (submitted 3 Oct 2026 by K. Juschenko; v1 only). The authors use a companion result, a finite-resolution form of the Rudolph-Johnson theorem, to bound low-frequency Fourier coefficients of a ×2×3-invariant measure by its normalised entropy at each resolution. They read this in reverse as a constraint on eigenfunctions in potential counterexamples. Theorems: (0.1) near return of e(x) under the semigroup forces small entropy at fine resolution; (0.2) adherence to ×2-eigenfunctions forces entropy decay; (0.3) torsion-eigenfunction version; (0.4) an eigencomponent cap. The authors write that 'our theorems should be interpreted as constraints on the class of potential counterexamples'. They do not prove the dichotomy; they say that if the conjecture is true the measures satisfying their hypotheses are atomic and the conclusions 'hold for trivial reasons'. AI (Section 2, 'Discussion of AI use'): 'The artificial intelligence models Claude Opus 4.8, Opus 5, Fable 5 and Fable 5.1 from Anthropic PBC were extensively used in the composition of this article.' Stated uses: 'to accelerate exclusion of incorrect ideas on the part of the authors' (falsification); 'to accelerate the accurate management of constants and parameters in proof design' (bookkeeping); 'to accelerate the identification of typographical errors in the Latex manuscript' (typography). 'Claude was called for additional verification and error-cleaning after every line.' 'The authors wrote the manuscript line-by-line in order to verify it themselves.' Quotes above come from a summarising fetch and were not checked against the PDF. None is placed in ai.systems; see summary.
events.delivers: Conditional entropy bounds for ×2×3-invariant measures under spectral hypotheses (near return of the coordinate function, adherence to ×2-eigenfunctions, torsion eigenfunctions, eigencomponent cap). Each is a constraint on counterexamples and does not classify measures. Restriction: the hypotheses are spectral and the bounds are asymptotic in resolution.
events.remains: The whole bullet. The authors do not settle either the Lebesgue side or the atomic side.
events.direction: Conditional and aimed at potential counterexamples: if any counterexample exists in the theorems' hypotheses, its entropy must be small or decay. It does not state or refute the conjecture.

events.what_happened: P. Burton and K. Juschenko, 'Rudolph-Johnson without dynamics: endomorphic rigidity on the circle', arXiv 2610.07317 (submitted 5 Oct 2026; v1 only). Per the abstract as summarised: entropy alone, with no invariance assumption, pushes a Borel probability measure on the circle toward Lebesgue measure under every sublacunary set of multipliers; the set includes the powers generated by 2 and 3. Some weak-star limit of the pushforwards dominates Lebesgue measure scaled by the upper entropy dimension; effective bounds are stated at finite entropy resolutions; there is an analogue of Lyons' conjecture that holds at full entropy dimension for sublacunary sets and fails for powers of 3. The authors call the semigroup case 'an invariance-free form of the Rudolph-Johnson theorem'. The abstract does not claim to prove the Furstenberg conjecture. This is probably the companion ('[4]') cited by arXiv 2610.04745 as proving a finite-resolution form of Rudolph-Johnson, but that is not confirmed: the bibliography of 2610.04745 was not readable.
events.delivers: An invariance-free, entropy-dimension-scaled domination of Lebesgue measure for weak-star limits of pushforwards under sublacunary multiplier sets (including the ×2, ×3 semigroup), with effective finite-resolution bounds. It does not assume joint invariance and does not classify invariant measures.
events.remains: The classification of ergodic jointly invariant measures.
events.direction: Toward Lebesgue-type rigidity under entropy, without invariance. It does not decide the classification.

events.what_happened: I. J. Aberkane, 'A Low-Tech Proof of Furstenberg's ×2–×3 Conjecture', HAL preprint hal-05122193 (PDF file name FurstenbergSierpinskyV7.pdf). The title and URL come from a search result. The landing page and PDF both returned an Anubis access-denied page, so the text, date, scope and claimed proof could not be read. A search summary describes the preprint as claiming a completely elementary proof; I could not confirm this. The title does not say whether the measure version or the set version is meant. No review, citation or comment was found in my searches.
events.delivers: Unknown: the paper could not be read. If the title means the measure version, the claim would settle the bullet; the title does not establish that.
events.remains: Unknown until the paper is read.
events.doubts: Could not open the preprint; the author and affiliation are unverified; I found no specialist reading or citation. A claimed short elementary proof of a problem described in 2026 sources as open for over 50 years would normally draw comment; none was found, but the search index may lag.
events.direction: Unknown: the claim may point toward the Lebesgue-or-finite side, but I could not confirm which version or which way.

disputes.summary: Dating of the conjecture is inconsistent across sources: the 1967 set-level theorem (Tal 2021); the measure conjecture dated to 1969 or 1970 in some sources; 'around 1970' in Hochman (2026). The bullet's measure form is not dated by any source I could read directly. No priority dispute on the measure question was found.

summary: Since 26 Jan 2024 no source I could read resolves or moves the measure classification, and the bullet remains open in every 2026 source I read. Two in-window papers are the closest, and both say the problem is open. (1) Hochman, arXiv 2609.21481 (18 Sep 2026): for non-atomic ergodic ×a-invariant measures on [0,1] with a, b multiplicatively independent, almost every point has a dense ×b-orbit, including in zero entropy. The author's own text says the problem 'remains open; ... nothing is known in entropy zero', and that a positive answer would not yield this theorem. This is a neighbouring statement, not a classification. The same result was announced in the HUJI talk 'Around the x2,x3 question' (5 May 2026); by the write-up rule it is dated to the arXiv version. (2) Burton and Juschenko, arXiv 2610.04745 (3 Oct 2026): conditional entropy-rate bounds for ×2×3-invariant measures under spectral hypotheses, framed by the authors as 'constraints on the class of potential counterexamples'; they say that if the conjecture holds the measures in their hypotheses are atomic 'for trivial reasons'. Their companion (apparently), arXiv 2610.07317 (5 Oct 2026), gives invariance-free, finite-resolution entropy-domination bounds for sublacunary multiplier sets including {2^k 3^l}; the link to [4] in 2610.04745 is not confirmed. Other in-window items are neighbouring: Algom (30 Aug 2026, dimension of projections of ×p-invariant measures on T^2), Zhao (25 Aug 2026, zero-entropy optimisers), Kravitz and Leng (Oct 2025, quantitative pyjama), Algom-Wu-Hochman (Oct 2024, embeddings), and Burton and Panangaden (30 Oct 2024, reformulations only; journal version 2026). Before 2024 the positive-entropy case is settled: Rudolph 1990 and Johnson 1992 (positive entropy for one map gives Lebesgue), with Lyons 1988 (K-mixing for one map gives Lebesgue) and Host 1995 (normality) as related results. The zero-entropy case, where a counterexample would have to live, is open in every source I read. Badea and Grivaux (2023, Discrete Analysis 2024) disprove a neighbouring Furstenberg conjecture on convergence of iterated pushforwards of T_p-invariant measures, not the classification. The shift from 'Lebesgue or atomic' in Wikipedia to 'finite support' in the ergodic literature is a wording point: I did not verify their equivalence in detail. The bullet's frozen Wikipedia link goes to Hillel Furstenberg's biography, which does not discuss the conjecture; I found no Wikipedia article on the conjecture itself (the guessed URL returned 404). AI. Two 2026 papers name AI systems, and in neither case did I place a system in ai.systems. In 2610.04745 the authors' Section 2 ('Discussion of AI use') says that 'The artificial intelligence models Claude Opus 4.8, Opus 5, Fable 5 and Fable 5.1 from Anthropic PBC were extensively used in the composition of this article'. The uses they state are falsification ('to accelerate exclusion of incorrect ideas on the part of the authors'), bookkeeping of constants in proof design, LaTeX typography, and 'additional verification and error-cleaning after every line'; they also write that 'the authors wrote the manuscript line-by-line in order to verify it themselves'. I scanned the rest of the text for any sentence crediting a model with a lemma, theorem or idea and found none. Each stated use is checking, bookkeeping or typography, which the protocol excludes from ai.systems. This is a close call: 'extensively used' and 'proof design' could be read as load-bearing, and the quotes come from a summarising fetch that I could not check against the PDF. In 2609.21481 the disclosure reads 'ChatGPT 5.6 Terra was used to help locate errata.' with corrections 'done out manually'. That is checking, so it is not in ai.systems. Across the AI searches (AlphaEvolve, OpenAI for Science, Epoch's FrontierMath open problems, Gemini Deep Think, AlphaProof, Harmonic's Aristotle, Axiom, and general 2026 'AI solves' news), I found no AI result on this problem. The openai/math repository (6 Oct 2026; 722 manuscripts in 372 families) was scanned end to end through its CONTENTS.md file by keyword; no entry concerns the ×2×3 problem, though the per-manuscript files were not read. A ProofAtlas listing of a 'Furstenberg's ×2, ×3 Conjecture' workspace gives no status, date, model or result, and I have not recorded it as an event. Where the call was close: (a) whether the 2610.04745 AI use is load-bearing (the record leaves ai.systems empty; the judging pass should weigh the authors' own wording); (b) whether Hochman's Theorem 1.2 is a case of the dichotomy (I read it as no, since it does not classify and the author says the problem is open); (c) whether 'atomic' and 'finitely supported' are the same class for ergodic measures (probably, not verified). The unopened HAL preprint by Aberkane, claiming a 'low-tech proof' of 'Furstenberg's ×2–×3 Conjecture', is the largest single unknown: if its claim is the measure version and correct, it would change the outcome; I could not read it, and the title alone does not settle which version it addresses.
competing_reading: The strongest case for a different reading is as follows. (1) Burton and Juschenko's theorems are unconditional bounds on entropy for measures satisfying spectral hypotheses, and the authors say that if the conjecture is true the hypotheses force atomicity. One could argue that together with the Rudolph-Johnson positive-entropy theorem, these results cover a large class of potential counterexamples, so the open part is smaller than 'the zero-entropy case'. The authors do not claim this, and the hypotheses are spectral, so I do not read it as a partial resolution. (2) Hochman's Theorem 1.2 holds for zero-entropy non-atomic ×a-invariant measures, which might be read as the zero-entropy case of the dichotomy. But the theorem does not assume ×b-invariance, the author says it does not settle the problem, and dense-orbit properties do not identify the measure. (3) The authors' statement that the models were 'extensively used in the composition of this article' could be read as making the 2610.04745 mathematics AI-assisted in a load-bearing way, which would put the paper in the AI category; the authors' own specific uses are checking and bookkeeping, and they state that they verified every line, so I do not read it that way. (4) The HAL 'low-tech proof' could be a complete solution of the measure version, in which case the outcome would be 'settled by a single human author, unreviewed'. I could not read it, so this reading is possible but unsupported by anything I could check.
what_would_settle_it: (a) Reading the Aberkane HAL preprint (hal-05122193) through a route that is not blocked: its date, whether it addresses the measure or the set version, and the argument's key step. (b) The bibliography of arXiv 2610.04745 (not readable by my tools) to confirm that [4] is arXiv 2610.07317. (c) The full text of arXiv 2609.21481 beyond the first 100k characters (the references and the last 8k were not read), to confirm whether it asserts any form of the dichotomy as open in the terms of the bullet. (d) The PDF text of 2610.04745's Section 2, to confirm the quotes against the source, and the authors' own statement of which results depend on the model's output. (e) Referee or expert reactions to 2610.04745 and 2609.21481, which would take weeks to months to appear. (f) The openai/math per-manuscript files for any manuscript with 'Furstenberg' or ×2×3 content, and the ProofAtlas workspace status. (g) Any written version of the Badea–Grivaux 'exceptional sets' results mentioned in the June 2024 and Feb 2026 talks.
